title: Brailix document IR
description: Serialized form of the text-side IR — DocumentIR.to_dict() (the root below). Block and inline nodes are each ONE union definition: the type tag is enumerated, and the properties are the union of every registered node's serialized fields. Which fields belong to which type is the dataclass registry's contract (brailix.ir.document / brailix.ir.inline) — duplicating that per-type here would be a third copy of the same rules. Optional/default fields are omitted from the wire form, never emitted as null. The document deliberately carries NO assets key: binary side-payloads never enter the text IR (ARCHITECTURE §1).

span.description: Half-open [start, end) code-point range. Block spans are source-document coordinates; inline spans are leaf-local.

tree.description: Serialized MathML — ET trees ride the JSON as XML strings. Spelled the same as a block's tree field, because it is the same thing. The one inline node that carries one; music and graphics reach the backend as blocks, which carry their own.

date_component.description: One <digits><marker> unit of a date (2026年 / 5月). A value object the date holds, not an inline node — no type tag, no registry entry.

reading.description: The marker's reading (年 → nián); the digits have none.

inlines.description: The typed tokens a leaf block's text became.

blocks.description: Nested blocks — a list's items, a table's rows, a row's cells. Which block class the entries must be is the owning class's own child_type declaration, enforced in both directions by the loader rather than restated here.

tree.description: Serialized domain tree — MathML for math_block, MusicXML for score / music_block, SVG for graphic. ET trees ride the JSON as XML strings.

version.description: Serialization format version. Enumerates exactly what DocumentIR.from_dict loads (brailix.ir.document._SUPPORTED_IR_VERSIONS — a test compares the two sets), so a payload this schema accepts is a payload the loader accepts. A future version joins both together with its migration.
